pairs.notes: A has better button differentiation (primary vs secondary style) and the Start→Resume label feedback; B's uniform button styling and missing label update make it feel less finished.
B's CSS custom properties, cleaner vertical stacking on mobile, and auto-mode-switch polish edge out A, whose global button:hover rule awkwardly overrides the mode-button active state.
B earns the full feature score with disabled mode buttons while running, a two-beep alert, and an accent-colored display; A's darker inactive mode button style diverges from the accent-forward spec.
B uses a 100ms interval with float accumulation (elapsedTime += 0.1), causing the MM:SS display to show fractional seconds (e.g. '24:59.9'); A implements all features correctly.
A merges Start and Pause into one button, failing the spec's explicit 'Start, Pause, and Reset buttons' requirement; B provides all three separately with an accent-colored display.
